title: China shuts for Mid-Autumn Festival holiday today, a preview of the week-long National Day gap to come
body: AUD is the most exposed of the major currencies. It usually trades partly as a proxy for China, and with onshore markets shut it loses that anchor and has to lean more on oil, Treasury yields and the RBA. With Dalian iron ore futures closed, iron ore price discovery shifts to the Singapore contract, which is thinner. Gold also loses one of its biggest sources of Asia-time demand. With the Shanghai Gold Exchange shut, Chinese physical and speculative buying steps aside, leaving prices more exposed to Treasury yields and the US dollar until mainland buyers return. Asian equity desks may see lighter volumes and wider spreads, so moves on single headlines can overshoot. Traders sometimes position ahead of long Chinese breaks by cutting exposure, which can add to price swings in the three sessions before National Day. After the holiday, the first sessions back can see catch-up moves as mainland markets react to a week of global news at once. --- China takes a long weekend now and a full week off in October, and each break leaves a bigger gap in the Asian session. Thin trading and a crowded news calendar can be a volatile mix.

title: New Zealand Dollar grinds lower as US bond yields climb to new highs
body: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) has its Official Cash Rate (OCR) at 2.75%, and markets now price at least a 75% chance that it goes to 3% on October 28, against about 30% right after the September 2 hike. NZD/USD is trading just above 0.5650, its lowest since late June.

body: The 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.50% on Thursday, and two Fed officials gave bond buyers no reason to expect relief. New York Fed President Williams said another rate increase this year looks reasonable, and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson said rates may need to rise a little more.

title: Pound Sterling slides again as Fed speakers go full hawkish
body: Bank of England (BoE) Deputy Governors Lombardelli and Breeden said on Thursday that they are moving closer to voting for a rate hike, and the Pound fell for a fourth straight session regardless. GBP/USD is trading just above 1.3200, its lowest in nearly three months.

title: Ibovespa Falls Amid External Pressures
body: The Ibovespa slipped 1% to close at 183,966 on Thursday, posting broad-based losses after a volatile session amid a deteriorating external backdrop. US Treasury yields surged to multi-decade highs as expectations increased for another Fed rate hike this year, while concerns over energy-driven inflation persisted. Crude oil prices and global bond yields were volatile late in the session, with a bias to the upside. In its Monetary Policy Report, the BCB noted that the recent oil price shock has not yet produced significant second-round inflation effects on the Brazilian economy, although it has had a direct impact on prices. The central bank also lowered its GDP growth forecast for 2026. At the same time, the federal government reduced the amount of funds frozen in the 2026 budget, despite lingering worries about high public spending. On the corporate front, financial stocks ended lower, with Banco do Brasil falling 2.8%. Utilities also weakened, with Axia down 1.6%. Vale shed 1.1% as rising freight costs weighed on Brazil's iron ore exports to Asia. Petrobras declined 0.7%, even in the face of higher international oil prices. title: U.S. Reserve Balances Edge Higher to $2.97 Trillion, Extending Liquidity Uptrend
body: Reserve balances held at Federal Reserve Banks in the United States increased to $2.969 trillion, up from the previous level of $2.921 trillion, according to data updated on 24 September 2026. The move reflects a continued rise in the liquidity parked by financial institutions at the central bank. The increase of $48 billion in reserve balances suggests that banks are maintaining substantial excess reserves within the Federal Reserve system rather than deploying all available funds into lending or other assets. While the data alone does not specify the underlying drivers, shifts in reserve balances are often monitored by market participants as an indicator of overall banking system liquidity and the stance of monetary conditions. With reserve balances remaining close to the $3 trillion mark, investors and analysts are likely to watch upcoming releases for signals on whether this trend persists, stabilizes, or reverses, as it may influence expectations around funding markets and broader financial conditions in the United States. title: Fed's Balance Sheet Edges Up to $6.748 Trillion, Signaling Ongoing Policy Caution
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet inched higher to $6.748 trillion, up slightly from $6.747 trillion previously, according to data updated on 24 September 2026. The marginal $1 billion increase suggests the central bank is maintaining a cautious policy stance while keeping overall asset levels largely stable. Although the move is modest in size, changes in the Fed's balance sheet are closely watched by investors as a gauge of underlying liquidity conditions and the central bank's broader monetary strategy. The latest figure indicates that, for now, the Fed is not embarking on aggressive expansion or rapid runoff of its holdings, reinforcing expectations for a steady, measured approach to balance sheet management in the near term. title: TSX Edges Lower as Mining Stocks Weigh
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index slipped 0.1% to close at 35,706 on Thursday, as weakness in mining and a muted financial sector weighed on the benchmark. Canada's 10-year government bond yield climbed to a three-year high, reflecting persistent energy-driven inflation concerns and a surge in US Treasury yields to multi-decade peaks. Crude oil and global bond yields were volatile but trended higher late in the session. Financials were little changed overall. Falling gold prices pressured mining names, with Agnico Eagle down 0.6% and Wheaton Precious Metals off 0.7%. Kinross tumbled 11.3% after cutting its production outlook for 2026 and 2027. By contrast, energy stocks advanced alongside higher oil prices. Retailers also moved higher, supported by estimates pointing to a rebound in August retail sales, which would mark the strongest monthly gain since January. Technology shares were mostly firmer, led by Shopify, which rose 2.4%, tracking gains in Meta as the two companies expand their partnership to allow purchases via Meta's Muse AI agent using Shop Pay. BlackBerry fell 3.9% despite reporting solid fiscal 2Q26 results. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stocks Mixed as Yields and Oil Stay Volatile
body: US stock indices ended Thursday mixed amid renewed volatility in both bond and oil markets. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq finished roughly flat, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined by 162 points. The yield on the 10-year US Treasury briefly surpassed 5.15% before easing back to around 5.1%, holding near its highest levels since 2007. The 30-year yield also climbed, reaching its strongest level since 2004. Borrowing costs rose in tandem with higher oil prices, driven by escalating tensions between the US and Iran. Later in the session, however, reports indicated that US and Iranian negotiators were moving closer to an agreement that would restore tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices subsequently pared gains, which helped pull yields on shorter-dated Treasuries lower. AI-focused hyperscalers delivered a mixed performance. Alphabet gained 1.3%, and Meta rallied 4.5%, supported by favorable reception to their new AI agent software and hardware launches. By contrast, Microsoft slipped 0.5%, and Amazon ended the session little changed. Oracle dropped 3.5% after declaring force majeure in connection with delays at a data center project in New Mexico. Chipmakers also traded mixed, weighed down in part by heavy debt issuance tied to financing AI infrastructure buildouts. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Banxico Holds Key Rate at 6.50% in September
body: Mexico's central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 6.50% at its September meeting, as widely anticipated by markets. The governing board said it evaluated the inflation outlook in light of exchange-rate movements, the differing positions of the Mexican and US business cycles, the lack of demand-side pressures in Mexico, and the current degree of monetary tightness. The headline inflation forecast for the third quarter of 2026 was revised down, reflecting lower-than-expected non-core inflation, while the core inflation projection was edged slightly higher. Overall, the balance of risks to the inflation outlook remains skewed to the upside. Ongoing changes in US economic policy and protracted geopolitical conflicts continue to cloud the outlook. At the same time, the Mexican economy is estimated to have slowed in the third quarter. Slack conditions are expected to persist over the entire forecast horizon, and downside risks to economic activity remain. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Oil Near $95 as Gulf Shipping Remains Disrupted
body: Crude oil hovered near $95 a barrel on Thursday, pulling back from an earlier spike to $97 amid indications that the United States and Iran may be moving toward a deal to restore Persian Gulf oil exports. Media reports said US and Iranian negotiators are exploring an agreement that would lift naval blockades on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz and ease US sanctions on Iran. The market had surged earlier after Iran-aligned Houthi militants in Yemen launched missile attacks on several Saudi cities, including Yanbu and Taif. Yanbu, on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, is a critical oil export terminal. As a result, Saudi Arabia's alternative export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz now faces war-risk insurance premiums nearly as high as those for tankers sailing directly through the strait. On Wednesday, only 10 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz, well below the 10-day moving average of 17, highlighting the disruption. In Washington, the US Senate narrowly voted down a nonbinding resolution calling for an end to the war with Iran, underscoring ongoing political divisions over the conflict.
